To act upon with a rake, or as if with a rake.
Often followed by in: to gather (things which are apart) together, especially quickly.

ex.en: The police raked through his life.
ex.ja: 警察は彼の生活に立ち入って調べ上げた。

note.ja: 古英語 raca（熊手）から。「熊手・かき集める」。

en: To feel resentment over; to consider as an affront.
To express displeasure or indignation at.

resent.ety: From Middle French ressentir, resentir, from Old French resentir (Modern ressentir), from re- + sentir (“to feel”).

ex.ja: 彼は彼女が弟とデートしていることに腹を立てた。

note.ja: rhetoric（修辞学）+ -al。ギリシャ語 rhētōr（弁論家）。「修辞的な」→ rhetorical question（答えを求めない反語的な問い）。

en: By right; by law.

rightful.ety: From Middle English rightful, ryghtfull, riȝtful, from Old English *rihtfull (suggested by derivative unrihtfull (“unrightful”)), equivalent to right + -ful.

treatise.ety: From Middle English tretys, from Anglo-Norman tretiz and Old French traitis (“treatise, account”), from traitier (“to deal with, treat”).

ex.ja: リストの「忘れられたワルツ第3番」は隠れた名曲だと思う。

en: Military equipment, especially weapons and ammunition.
Artillery.

The flesh or fur of this animal

ex.en: I saw an otter.

ex.en: I saw some otters.
ex.ja: カワウソを見たよ。

ex.ja: ラッコは背泳ぎをしながら蛤を食べるのが大好きです。

The sound so produced.

To add color or pigment to something.

ex.ja: 私の心と思いとを練り清めてください。

ex.en: Being a teacher, you must learn to keep a tight rein on your emotions.
ex.ja: 君は一人の教師なんだから、自分の感情を厳しくコントロールできるようにならなければならない。

A thumbtack.
To nail (something) with a tack (small nail with a flat head).
To sew/stitch with a tack (loose seam used to temporarily fasten pieces of cloth).

en: A paste, normally used with a toothbrush, for cleaning the teeth.
To cover, or smear, with toothpaste.

toothpaste.ety: From tooth + paste. Remaining for only a brief time.
Something that is transient.

transient.ety: From Late Latin transiēnt- (for classical transeunt-), stem of transiēns, present participle of trānsīre (“to go over, to pass”).

ex.ja: 人の人生は、はかないものだ。

Rejoicing in victory or success; displaying triumph; exultant.

To decide as an umpire.

ex.ja: 私はその試合の審判をするように頼まれた。

To prospect for gold by manually digging holes into overlying earth, as into a hillside.

coyote.ety: Borrowed from Spanish coyote, from a Nahuan language, from Proto-Nahuan *koyoo-tl. Compare Chinook ki-o-tī.

note.ja: ナワトル語（アステカの言語）coyotl からスペイン語を経た語。

en: That cripples or incapacitates
Causing a severe and insurmountable problem; detrimental.
The act by which somebody or something is crippled.

note.ja: cripple + -ing。「深刻な打撃を与える」。

en: To furnish with decorations.
To improve the appearance of an interior of, as a house, room, or office.

decorate.ety: From Middle English decorat (“adorned”), from Latin decorātus, perfect passive participle of decorō (“to adorn, distinguish, honor”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from decus (“ornament, grace, dignity, honor”, decor- in compounds), akin to decor (“elegance, grace, beauty, ornament”), from decet (“adorn, befit”).

ex.en: I like to decorate my room with flowers.
ex.ja: 私は部屋を花で飾るのが好きだ。

ex.en: My wife showed excellent taste in decorating the room.
ex.ja: 私の妻は部屋を飾るときに優れた美的感覚を発揮した。

ex.en: I like to decorate my apartment to suit my taste.
ex.ja: 私は好みに合わせてアパートを飾るのが好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 decorare（飾る）から。decus（飾り）。「飾る・勲章を与える」。decoration と同じ。

en: Eligible to be deducted.
An amount of expenses that must be paid out of pocket before an insurer will pay further expenses.

ex.en: You are covered with a $300 deductible.
ex.ja: ３００ドルの免責額の保険でカバーされます。

ex.en: Your contribution to the school is tax-deductible.
ex.ja: 学校に対するあなたの寄付は、所得控除の対象になる。

note.ja: deduct（差し引く）+ -ible。「控除できる」→ 保険の「免責額」。

en: Joining two nonadjacent vertices (of a polygon or polyhedron).
Having slanted or oblique lines or markings.
A line joining non-adjacent vertices of a polygon.
A line or plane at an oblique angle to another.

diagonal.ety: From Middle French diagonal, from Latin diagōnālis, from Ancient Greek διαγώνιος (diagṓnios, “from angle to angle”), from διά (diá, “across”) + γωνία (gōnía, “angle”).

ex.en: Cut the cloth in a diagonal direction.
ex.ja: 布を斜めに裁ちなさい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diagōnios ＝ dia（通して）+ gōnia（角）。「角から角へ通る」→「対角線の」。pentagon と同じ gōnia。

zh: 敗壞 /败坏 名聲 /名声

en: To harm the good reputation of (a person).
To cause (an idea or piece of evidence) to seem false or unreliable.
Discrediting or disbelieving.
A person or thing that causes harm to a reputation, as of a person, family, or institution.

en: An item of kitchen furniture, like a cabinet with shelves, for storing crockery or utensils.
An item of bedroom furniture, like a low chest of drawers (bureau), often with a mirror.

dresser.ety: From Middle English dressure, dressor, dressour, a borrowing from Old French drecëur, drecëure, from the verb dresser.

ex.en: The mirror is on top of the dresser.
ex.ja: 鏡は鏡台の上にあります。

ex.en: This dresser takes up too much room.
ex.ja: この化粧台は場所を取りすぎる。

ex.en: "Where's my phone?" "It's on the dresser!"
ex.ja: 「携帯、どこかしら？」「鏡台の上だよ！」

note.ja: dress（服を着せる・整える）+ -er。「鏡台・整理だんす」、「着こなす人」。

en: A tree of the genus Ulmus of the family Ulmaceae, large deciduous trees with alternate stipulate leaves and small apetalous flowers.
Wood from an elm tree.

elm.ety:
From Middle English elme, elm, from Old English elm, from Proto-West Germanic *elm, from Proto-Germanic *elmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁élem (“mountain elm”).
See also dialectal Low German Elm, dialectal German Ilm, archaic German Ilme, Norwegian and Swedish alm; also Irish leamh, Latin ulmus, Albanian ulzë (“maple”).

note.ja: 古英語 elm から。ラテン語 ulmus と同じ祖先。「ニレ」。

enquiry.ety: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). The alternative form inquiry was subsequently respelled to conform to the original Latin spelling, as opposed to the Old French spelling.

note.ja: en（中へ）+ quir（求める）+ y。inquiry のイギリス式綴り →「問い合わせ・調査」。

en: Marked by or having equity.
Fair, just, or impartial.

equitable.ety: From French équitable, from Old French, from equité (“equity”).

ex.en: They argue that the distribution of wealth should be equitable.
ex.ja: 富の分配は公平でなければならないと彼らは言う。

note.ja: equity（公平）+ -able。ラテン語 aequus（等しい）。「公平な」。equal と同じ。

en: To make use of, to apply, especially of something nonmaterial; to bring to bear.
To put in vigorous action.

exert.ety: From Latin exsertus, past participle of exserō (“to stretch or thrust forth or out”), from ex- + serō (“to string together”).

ex.en: You should exert yourself to get better results.
ex.ja: もっといい成績を得るように努力しなさい。

ex.en: Several politicians exerted strong pressure on the committee.
ex.ja: 数人の政治家が委員会に強い圧力をかけた。

ex.en: We exerted ourselves to finish the job.
ex.ja: 私たちはその仕事を仕上げようと努力した。

note.ja: ラテン語 exserere（突き出す）から。ex + serere（つなぐ）。「（力を）出す・行使する」。insert と同じ。

en: The condition of being happy.
Intense happiness.

felicity.ety: From Middle English felicite (“bliss, happiness, joy; delight, pleasure; a source of happiness; good fortune; prosperity; well-being; of a planet: in an influential position”) [and other forms], borrowed from Old French felicité (modern French félicité (“bliss, happiness; felicity”)), from Latin fēlīcitātem, the accusative singular of fēlīcitās (“fertility, fruitfulness; happiness, felicity; good fortune; success”), from fēlīx (“happy; blessed, fortunate, lucky; fertile, fruitful; prosperous; auspicious, favourable”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)- (“to nurse, suckle”)) + -itās

note.ja: ラテン語 felicitas（幸福）から。felix（幸運な）。「至福」。Felix（人名：幸運な人）と同じ。

en: Of, or relating to feudalism.

feudal.ety: From Old French feodal, from Medieval Latin feodalis, from feodum, feudum, fevum (“fief, fee”), from Frankish *fehu (“cattle, owndom, property, fee”), from Proto-Germanic *fehu (“cattle”). By surface analysis, feud (“estate”) + -al. More at fee.

ex.en: It seems a bit feudal to call him "sir".
ex.ja: 彼を「サー」と呼ぶのは少し封建的に思える。

ex.en: In feudal Japan, the lord with the largest land holdings was called a "daimyo."
ex.ja: 日本の封建時代には、最大の土地を所有した領主は「大名」と呼ばれた。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 feudum（封土）から。「封建的な」。fee（料金・封土）と同じ語源。

en: Made flat by something.

note.ja: flatten（平らにする）+ -ed。flat と同じ。

en: Hair or wool of a sheep or similar animal.
Insulating skin with the wool attached.
To con or trick (someone) out of money.
To cut off the fleece from (a sheep or other animal).

fleece.ety: From Middle English fles, flees, flese, from Old English flēos, flīes, flȳs, from Proto-West Germanic *fleus.

ex.en: Mary had a little lamb whose fleece was white as snow.
ex.ja: メリーさんは、雪のように真っ白な毛をした子羊を飼っていました。

ex.en: Mary had a little lamb, whose fleece was white as snow.
ex.ja: メリーさんは、雪のように真っ白な毛をした子羊を飼っていました。

note.ja: 古英語 flēos（羊毛）から。「羊毛」→ 羊毛を刈るように金を巻き上げる →「だまし取る」。

en: Food for animals; that which is fed to cattle, horses, and sheep, such as hay, cornstalks, vegetables, etc.
A load: various English units of weight or volume based upon standardized cartloads of certain commodities, generally around 1000 kg.

fodder.ety:
From Middle English fodder, foder, from Old English fōdor (“feed; fodder”), from Proto-West Germanic *fōdr, from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą, from *fōdô (“food”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to guard, graze, feed”).
Compare Saterland Frisian Fodder, West Frisian foer, Dutch voer (“pasture; fodder”), German Futter (“fodder; feed”), Danish foder, Swedish foder. More at food.

note.ja: 古英語 fōdor（飼料）から。food、feed と同じ祖先。「飼料」→ cannon fodder（使い捨ての兵）。

en: To handle nervously or awkwardly.
To grope awkwardly in trying to find something
The dropping of a ball by accident.
A clumsy sexual encounter.

fumble.ety:
From late Middle English, from Low German fummeln, fommeln, fammeln (German fummeln), or Dutch fommelen.
Or, perhaps from a Scandinavian/North Germanic source; compare related Old Norse fálma, Icelandic fálma, Danish fumle, especially Swedish fumla, famla, with variants: fumbla (“fumble”), fambla (“famble”), related to Swedish fim, fem (Danish fim, Norwegian fim, feima), with a root meaning of “cover, coating of foam or figuratively ditto”, cognate to German Feim (“surf”) and English foam. Possibly has (a more or less unconscious) connection to fathom (via Old Norse faðmr, Swedish famn) in the

ex.en: She fumbled with a piece of paper.
ex.ja: あやふやな手つきで一枚の紙を動かした。

ex.en: She fumbled with the glasses as she brought them in.
ex.ja: 怪しげな手つきで彼女はグラスを運んできた。

note.ja: 低地ドイツ語 fommeln（手探りする）とされる。「手探りする」→「（ボールを）落とす」。

en: An intense, blinding light.
Showy brilliance; gaudiness.
To stare angrily.
To shine brightly.
smooth and bright or translucent; glary

glare.ety: From Middle English glaren, from Old English *glærian, from Proto-West Germanic *glarōn. Cognate with dialectal Middle Dutch glariën (“to glisten; sparkle”), Low German glaren (“to shine brightly; glow; burn”), Middle High German glaren (“to shine brightly”). Related to glower, glass.

ex.en: The sudden glare hurt his eyes.
ex.ja: 突然の強い光を受けて彼の目は痛いほどだった。

ex.en: There's a lot of glare.
ex.ja: 太陽の照り返しが強い。

ex.en: I felt everyone's glare land on me all at once.
ex.ja: 一斉にいやな視線が降りかかって来た。

note.ja: 中英語 glaren（ぎらぎら光る）から。glass と同系。「ぎらぎら光る」→「にらみつける」。

en: Fine; of superior quality.
A connoisseur in eating and drinking; someone who takes their food seriously.

gourmet.ety: Borrowed from French gourmet, from Middle French gourmet, from Old French groumet (“wine broker, valet in charge of wines, servant”) from groume, grommes (“wine-taster, manservant”), apparently from Middle English grom, grome (“boy, valet, servant”), from Old English *grōm (“male child, boy, youth”), akin to Old English grōwan (“to grow”). Cognate of Spanish grumete and Catalan grumet. More at groom.

note.ja: フランス語 gourmet（ワインの鑑定人）から。「食通」。

en: The grasping of hands by two people when greeting, leave-taking, or making an agreement.
An exchange of signals between two devices when communications begin in order to ensure synchronization.
To perform a handshake; to shake hands.
To perform a handshake with another device.

handshake.ety: From hand + shake. See the appendix for the history of the gesture itself.

ex.en: He has a good firm handshake.
ex.ja: 彼はしっかりとした握手をする。

ex.en: He put out his hand to me for a handshake.
ex.ja: 彼は握手を求めて手を差し出した。

ex.en: When my father was offered a golden handshake, he took it.
ex.ja: 僕の父は早く退職するよう退職金を差し出されて受け取ったんだ。

note.ja: hand（手）+ shake（振ること）。「握手」。

en: With heft; heavy, strong, vigorous, mighty, impressive
Strong; bulky.

hefty.ety:
19th century. From heft (“weight”) + -y.
The similarity with German heftig (“vigorous, violent, intense”) is apparently coincidental. From the German are Dutch, Danish, Norwegian heftig, Swedish häftig.

note.ja: heft（重さ）+ -y。heave（持ち上げる）と同系。「重い・多額の」。

en: Made from or with herbs.
Made from natural herbs specifically as opposed to from synthetic materials.
A manual of herbs and their medical uses.
An herbal supplement.

herbal.ety: borrowed from Old French herbal. By surface analysis, herb + -al

ex.en: If you continue to take this herbal medicine, it will do you good.
ex.ja: この漢方薬を飲み続ければ効くでしょう。

note.ja: herb（ハーブ）+ -al。ラテン語 herba（草）。「ハーブの」。

en: A teenager who imitated the beatniks.
Someone who dresses in a hippie style.
Of or pertaining to hippies.
Not conforming to generally accepted standards.

hippie.ety: First use appears c. 1948. A usually disparaging variant of hipster. See also etymology of hippie.

note.ja: hip（流行に通じた）+ -ie。1960年代の反体制的な若者。

en: A mound of earth.
A speed bump or speed hump.
To bend something into a hump.
To carry (something), especially with some exertion.

hump.ety:
Probably borrowed from Dutch homp (“hump, lump”) or Middle Low German hump (“heap, hill, stump”), from Old Saxon *hump (“hill, heap, thick piece”), from Proto-Germanic *humpaz (“hip, height”), from Proto-Indo-European *kumb- (“curved”). Compare Proto-Germanic *huppōną (“to hop”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewb-, *ḱewb- (unnasalised root), and English hub (a softened variant without nasal?).
Cognate with West Frisian hompe (“lump, chunk”), Icelandic huppur (“flank”), Welsh cwm (“a hollow”), Latin incumbō (“to lie down”), Albanian sumbull (“round button, bud”), Ancient Greek κύμβη (kúmbē, “bowl”

ex.en: This job gives me the hump.
ex.ja: この仕事には憂鬱になる。

ex.en: Camels have either one or two humps.
ex.ja: ラクダには一つか二つのこぶがある。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「こぶ」。over the hump（峠を越えて）。

Having the quality of idiocy; very foolish

A constriction of the hernial sac, rendering it irreducible, but not great enough to cause strangulation.

en: Sexual relations between close relatives, especially immediate family members and sometimes first cousins, usually considered taboo.
Romantic relationships between close relatives, also widely taboo.
To engage in incestuous sexual activities.

incest.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin incestus. Displaced Old English mǣġhǣmed (literally “relative-sex”). Doublet of inchaste.

ex.en: Incest is a taboo found in almost all cultures.
ex.ja: 近親相姦はほとんど全ての文化において禁忌とされている。

note.ja: ラテン語 incestus（不浄な）から。in（否定）+ castus（純潔な）。chaste と同じ。

en: To bring (the body or part of it) into contact with a substance that causes illness (a pathogen), so that the pathogen begins to act on t…
To contaminate (an object or substance) with a pathogen.

infect.ety: From Middle French infect, from Latin infectus, perfect passive participle of inficiō (“dye, taint”).

ex.en: Infect the area with cholera.
ex.ja: コレラで地域を汚染する。

note.ja: in（中に）+ fect（作用する）。中に入り込んで作用する →「感染させる・影響する」。

The distal end of attachment of a muscle to a bone that will be moved by the muscle.

en: The act of interrupting, or the state of being interrupted.
the act of breaking into someone else’s speech.

interruption.ety: From Middle English interrupcioun, from Old French interrupcion, from Latin interruptio.

ex.en: I was annoyed with him for his interruptions.
ex.ja: 彼が度々口をはさむので腹がたった。

ex.en: Sorry for the interruption.
ex.ja: お邪魔しました。

ex.en: Discussion resumed after a short interruption.
ex.ja: ちょっと中断したあとで討議が再び始まった。

note.ja: inter（間に）+ rupt（破る）+ ion。間に割り込んで破ること →「中断・邪魔」。

en: A complicated or clandestine plot or scheme intended to effect some purpose by secret artifice; conspiracy; stratagem; the practice of en…
Clandestine intercourse between persons; illicit intimacy; a liaison or affair.
To conceive or carry out a secret plan intended to harm; to form a plot or scheme.
To arouse the interest of; to fascinate.

intrigue.ety: Borrowed from French intrigue, from Italian intricare, from Latin intrīcō (“to entangle, perplex, embarrass”). Doublet of intricate.

ex.en: Foreign people intrigue me.
ex.ja: 外国人って面白いなあ。

ex.en: He watches for an opportunity to intrigue against his rival.
ex.ja: 彼は競争相手を落とし入れようと虎視眈々としている。

note.ja: イタリア語 intrigare（もつれさせる）から。ラテン語 intricare。「もつれ」→「陰謀」→ 心をもつれさせる →「興味をそそる」。intricate と同じ。

en: A sensation felt on an area of the skin that causes a person or animal to want to scratch said area.
A constant teasing desire or want.
To feel itchy; to feel a need to be scratched.
To have a constant, teasing urge; to feel strongly motivated; to want or desire something.

itch.ety: From Middle English icche, ȝicche, from Old English ġiċċe (“itch”), from Proto-Germanic *jukjǭ (“itch”), of unknown origin. Cognate with Scots yeuk (“itch, itchiness”), Dutch jeuk (“itch”), German jucken.

ex.en: She had an itch to see her child.
ex.ja: 彼女は子供に会いたくてたまらなかった。

ex.en: My leg itches. I think something bit me.
ex.ja: 足が痒いよ。何かに噛まれたみたい。

ex.en: I have an itch in my ear.
ex.ja: 耳がかゆいのです。

note.ja: 古英語 giccan（かゆい）から。「かゆみ」→「むずむずする欲求」。
